rule: adoptable: both exact routes accept the view, its side is at most U and at most today's drawn side, row 10 admits it, it is the view its run draws, and it improves on today's drawing under the policy's improvement rule (docs/project/policies/regularization-policy.md#11-the-improvement-rule): A view improves on a drawing when it is worse than the drawing on none of the goals and better on at least one. Ties on the other goals are fine, and a tie on every goal is no improvement. The goals: light squares: fewer is better; uneven squares: fewer is better; near-axis squares: fewer is better; angle classes: fewer is better; hues: fewer is better; house total of full shared sides: more is better; stage total of full shared sides: more is better; exact side: smaller is better; exactness: exactly verified is better than numerically checked. Chosen: the first adoptable view (Evan Daniel's, then grid-slack by rising threshold) that no other adoptable view dominates
